text: The hand of the LORD came upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; and it was full of bones.
He led me all around them, and I saw that there were very many of them on the floor of the valley, and they were very dry.
He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, you know."
Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: I am going to put breath in you, and you will live.
I will fasten sinews on you, make flesh grow over you, cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied there was a sound, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
I looked, and there were sinews on them; flesh had grown, and skin had covered them over. But there was no breath in them.

Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, that they may live."
So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them. They came to life and stood on their feet—an army, vast beyond measure.

versions.text: So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them. They came to life and stood on their feet, a vast army.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew doubles מְאֹד for strong emphasis ("very, very great"). Adding an intensifier better conveys the climactic force and reads well aloud.

text: Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. See how they say, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is gone; we are cut off.'
Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to open your graves and bring you up out of them, my people, and I will bring you home to the land of Israel.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up out of them, my people.
I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live; and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it, declares the LORD."

versions.text: I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live; and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: The direct speech opened with a quotation mark in verse 11 is never closed. A closing quotation mark is needed at the end of this speech unit for consistency.

text: The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and all the house of Israel associated with him.'
Join them together, one to the other, into a single stick, so that they become one in your hand.
And when your people ask you, 'Won't you tell us what you mean by this?'

say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, together with the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will join them to the stick of Judah, making them one stick, so that they become one in my hand.
Hold the sticks on which you have written where they can see them,
and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to take the Israelites out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them into their own land.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Never again will they be two nations or be divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols and detestable images and all their transgressions. I will save them from all the places where they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my judgments and keep my statutes and carry them out.

versions.text: My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my judgments and be careful to keep my statutes.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has three verbs: walk in my judgments, keep my statutes, and do them. Collapsing the last two into "be careful to keep" drops the explicit note of performance (וְעָשׂוּ אוֹתָם).

text: They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They and their children and their children's children will live there forever, and David my servant will be their prince forever.
I will make a covenant of peace with them, an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary among them forever.
My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary stands among them forever."

versions.text: Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary stands among them forever.
versions.explanation: The quotation opened in verse 16 ("Son of man, take a stick...") is never closed; a closing quotation mark belongs at the end of this speech.
